{"id": "aristotle:good_temper:excess", "reasoning": "Irascibility is the excess of good temper: anger that flares too quickly, too often, and at the wrong things. Today this is the hot-tempered person who is easily provoked.", "labels": ["irascible", "hot-tempered"], "gloss": "This means flying into anger quickly and often, at trivial or wrongly chosen targets.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:truthfulness:deficiency", "reasoning": "Mock modesty is the deficiency of truthfulness: disclaiming or understating one's own real merits. Today this is the person who falsely plays down their achievements, fishing for praise or hiding behind feigned humility.", "labels": ["self-deprecating", "falsely modest"], "gloss": "This means understating your own merits and achievements, disclaiming credit you have actually earned.", "polysemy": true},
{"id": "aristotle:truthfulness:mean", "reasoning": "Truthfulness is the mean of presenting oneself accurately in word and deed. The truthful person is honest about who they are, claiming neither more nor less than is so.", "labels": ["truthful"], "gloss": "This means representing yourself accurately in speech and conduct, neither inflating nor understating what you are.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:truthfulness:excess", "reasoning": "Boastfulness is the excess of truthfulness: claiming merits one lacks or exaggerating those one has. Today this is the boastful person who brags.", "labels": ["boastful", "bragging"], "gloss": "This means claiming achievements you do not have, or inflating the ones you do have.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:ready_wit:deficiency", "reasoning": "Boorishness is the deficiency of ready wit: making no jokes and resenting those who do. Today this is the humorless, stiff person who takes teasing as an insult.", "labels": ["humorless", "boorish"], "gloss": "This means refusing to joke and bristling at others' banter, as if their wit were aimed at you.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:ready_wit:mean", "reasoning": "Ready wit is the mean of tasteful, well-measured joking in relaxed company. The witty person is quick with amusing remarks that suit the moment and do not hurt.", "labels": ["witty"], "gloss": "This means joking well, with taste and proportion, and enjoying lighthearted company without causing hurt.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:ready_wit:excess", "reasoning": "Buffoonery is the excess of ready wit: clowning for laughs at any cost, with no regard for decency or for whoever is the butt of the joke. Today this is the buffoon or clown.", "labels": ["buffoon", "clown"], "gloss": "This means playing the fool for laughs at any cost, careless of decency and of whom the joke wounds.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:friendliness:deficiency", "reasoning": "Quarrelsomeness is the deficiency of friendliness: contradicting everyone and not caring how much pain one causes in company. Today this is the argumentative, combative person.", "labels": ["quarrelsome", "contrarian"], "gloss": "This means opposing whatever others say and not minding how much discomfort it causes in company.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:friendliness:mean", "reasoning": "Friendliness is the mean of being pleasant in company, agreeing and objecting in the right measure. The friendly person is warm and easy to be with without flattering or fighting.", "labels": ["amiable", "friendly"], "gloss": "This means being pleasant company, agreeing and objecting in measure, without flattering or quarreling.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:friendliness:excess", "reasoning": "Obsequiousness is the excess of friendliness: praising everything and never objecting to spare others pain, and when done for gain it is flattery. Today this is the fawning, servile flatterer.", "labels": ["obsequious", "sycophantic"], "gloss": "This means praising everything and never objecting, so as to spare pain, and flattering for personal gain.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:modesty:deficiency", "reasoning": "Shamelessness is the deficiency of modesty: feeling no shame at all, even at disgraceful acts. Today this is the brazen person who is unembarrassed by disgrace.", "labels": ["shameless", "brazen"], "gloss": "This means feeling no shame whatsoever, even when one commits acts that are disgraceful.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:modesty:mean", "reasoning": "Modesty is the mean of feeling shame in due measure at what is disgraceful. The modest person blushes at real disgrace and is not troubled by innocent matters.", "labels": ["modest"], "gloss": "This means feeling shame in due measure at disgraceful conduct, and not at things that are innocent.", "polysemy": true},
{"id": "aristotle:modesty:excess", "reasoning": "Bashfulness is the excess of modesty: being ashamed of everything too easily and too much. Today this is the person who is easily embarrassed and shy.", "labels": ["bashful", "easily embarrassed"], "gloss": "This means blushing and feeling ashamed at almost everything, far too readily and too intensely.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:righteous_indignation:deficiency", "reasoning": "Spite is the deficiency of righteous indignation: feeling too little pain at others' undeserved good fortune that one rejoices in their misfortune. Today this is the malicious, spiteful person.", "labels": ["spiteful", "malicious"], "gloss": "This means taking pleasure in others' bad luck and feeling no pain when undeserved good luck comes their way.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:righteous_indignation:mean", "reasoning": "Righteous indignation is the mean of being pained at undeserved good fortune. The person with it resents injustice in others' success while accepting what is deserved.", "labels": ["righteous indignation"], "gloss": "This means feeling pained when good fortune reaches people who do not deserve it, and not when they do.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:righteous_indignation:excess", "reasoning": "Envy is the excess of righteous indignation: being pained by every good fortune of others, deserved or not. Today this is the envious person who resents others' success.", "labels": ["envious", "resentful"], "gloss": "This means being pained by every good thing that happens to others, whether they deserve it or not.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:dignity:deficiency", "reasoning": "Self-will is the deficiency of dignity: living with no regard for others and ignoring what they want. Today this is the headstrong, inconsiderate person who does as they please.", "labels": ["self-willed", "headstrong"], "gloss": "This means ignoring what others want and living as you please, with no account taken of anyone else.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:dignity:mean", "reasoning": "Dignity is the mean of keeping a proper measure of regard for others, neither ignoring nor serving them. The dignified person carries self-respect while respecting others.", "labels": ["dignified"], "gloss": "This means giving others their due regard, neither ignoring them nor living only to please them.", "polysemy": true},
{"id": "aristotle:dignity:excess", "reasoning": "Subservience is the excess of dignity: adjusting everything to others' wishes and living only to please them. Today this is the servile, obsequious person who has no will of their own.", "labels": ["subservient", "servile"], "gloss": "This means bending everything to others' wishes and living only to please them, with no will of one's own.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:practical_wisdom:deficiency", "reasoning": "Simpleness is the deficiency of practical wisdom: lacking the shrewdness to see how to reach one's ends, so one is easily taken in. Today this is the trusting, gullible person who is easily deceived.", "labels": ["naive", "gullible"], "gloss": "This means lacking the shrewdness to see how to reach one's goals, so that others easily deceive one.", "polysemy": true}
]}

{"rows": [
{"id": "aristotle:practical_wisdom:mean", "reasoning": "Practical wisdom is the mean between simpleness and rascality: the capacity to deliberate well about what is good for a whole human life and how to achieve it. A person who has it is sound in judgment about how to live and act, which today we call sagacity.", "labels": ["sagacious", "prudent"], "gloss": "This means judging well what is good for a whole human life and how to reach it.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "aristotle:practical_wisdom:excess", "reasoning": "Rascality is the excess of practical wisdom: skill at reaching any end, good or bad, without moral restraint. Today this is a person who is clever and calculating but has no scruples about how they get what they want.", "labels": ["unscrupulous", "crafty"], "gloss": "This means using cleverness to reach any goal at all, good or bad, with no moral restraint.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:01:dissembling", "reasoning": "Theophrastus' dissembler hides his real thoughts and plans behind friendly words and pretends to know or intend nothing. Today this is a duplicitous person whose manner conceals what they are really up to.", "labels": ["duplicitous", "dissembling"], "gloss": "This means hiding one's real aims behind friendly words while feigning ignorance of any plan.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:02:flattery", "reasoning": "The flatterer praises and fawns on someone in order to profit by it, not from genuine admiration. Today this is a sycophant who ingratiates themselves for gain.", "labels": ["sycophantic", "fawning"], "gloss": "This means praising and fawning over someone to gain something from them, not from honest admiration.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:03:garrulity", "reasoning": "The garrulous man pours out long, rambling talk on trivial matters to anyone who cannot get away. Today this is a long-winded talker who bores captive listeners.", "labels": ["garrulous", "long-winded"], "gloss": "This means rambling on at length about trivia to anyone unable to escape the conversation.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:04:boorishness", "reasoning": "The boor is ignorant of social manners and is coarse, uncouth and loud in company. Today this is a person who lacks polish and offends people through crude behavior.", "labels": ["boorish", "uncouth"], "gloss": "This means lacking social polish, being coarse, loud and rude in company.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:05:complaisance", "reasoning": "The complaisant man tries to please everyone and give no offense, agreeing with all sides. Today this is an obsequious person whose eagerness to please has become servile and spineless.", "labels": ["obsequious", "complaisant"], "gloss": "This means eagerly pleasing everyone, agreeing with every side, and avoiding any offense.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:06:recklessness", "reasoning": "Theophrastus' reckless man has lost all sense of shame or scruple in word and deed and will do anything disreputable. Today this is a brazen person with no principles restraining them.", "labels": ["brazen", "unprincipled"], "gloss": "This means feeling no shame in word or deed and readily doing anything disreputable.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:07:loquacity", "reasoning": "The loquacious man talks incessantly, cannot hold his tongue, interrupts and holds forth. Today this is someone who dominates conversation and cannot stop talking.", "labels": ["loquacious", "talkative"], "gloss": "This means talking incessantly, unable to hold one's tongue, interrupting others and holding forth.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:08:rumor_mongering", "reasoning": "The rumor-monger invents news and rumors and passes them on as fact. Today this is a person who spreads falsehoods as if they were true, which is more than idle gossip.", "labels": ["rumormonger", "gossip"], "gloss": "This means inventing news and rumors and passing them off as established fact.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:09:shamelessness", "reasoning": "The shameless man disregards his reputation for petty gain, such as cheating creditors or sponging off others. Today this is a disreputable person who will sink to small swindles and freeloading.", "labels": ["shameless", "disreputable"], "gloss": "This means discarding one's good name for petty gain, such as cheating creditors or freeloading.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:10:penuriousness", "reasoning": "The penurious man is excessively economical over tiny sums and counts every coin. Today this is a stingy person who grudges even trivial spending.", "labels": ["stingy", "penurious"], "gloss": "This means guarding even trivial sums so closely that one counts every coin.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:11:grossness", "reasoning": "The gross man openly commits offensive indecency and tells coarse jokes in public. Today this is a vulgar person with no sense of decorum, who flaunts crudeness.", "labels": ["vulgar", "crude"], "gloss": "This means openly flaunting offensive indecency and telling coarse jokes in public.", "polysemy": true},
{"id": "theophrastus:12:unseasonableness", "reasoning": "The man of poor timing chooses the wrong moment for everything, to the annoyance of those he deals with. Today this is a tactless person who lacks a sense of when to speak or act.", "labels": ["tactless", "poorly timed"], "gloss": "This means picking the wrong moment for everything, irritating the people one deals with.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:13:officiousness", "reasoning": "The officious man is overeager to help, promise and interfere, though his zeal is well meant. Today this is a meddlesome person who intrudes where help is unwanted.", "labels": ["officious", "meddlesome"], "gloss": "This means eagerly offering help, making promises and interfering where it is unwanted.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:14:stupidity", "reasoning": "Theophrastus' stupid man is slow of mind in word and act, forgetting things and missing the point. Today this is a slow-witted person who grasps things poorly.", "labels": ["slow-witted", "obtuse"], "gloss": "This means being slow to grasp things, forgetting easily, and missing the point in word and action.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:15:surliness", "reasoning": "The surly man is rude and ungracious in speech and refuses ordinary courtesy. Today this is a churlish, bad-tempered person who treats others with contempt.", "labels": ["surly", "churlish"], "gloss": "This means being rude and ungracious in speech, refusing even ordinary courtesy.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:16:superstition", "reasoning": "The superstitious man is cowardly toward the supernatural, fussing over omens, rites and pollution. Today this is a person governed by irrational fear of the supernatural.", "labels": ["superstitious", "fearful"], "gloss": "This means being frightened of the supernatural, fussing over omens, rites and ritual pollution.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:17:grumbling", "reasoning": "The grumbler finds unreasonable fault with his lot and complains even about favors he receives. Today this is a querulous person who is never satisfied.", "labels": ["querulous", "complaining"], "gloss": "This means finding fault with one's lot unreasonably, complaining even about favors received.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "theophrastus:18:distrust", "reasoning": "The distrustful man presumes everyone dishonest and checks up on all. Today this is a suspicious person who cannot take others at their word.", "labels": ["distrustful", "suspicious"], "gloss": "This means assuming everyone is dishonest and constantly checking up on people.", "polysemy": false}
]}

{"id": "via:judgment:underuse", "reasoning": "Judgment is the strength of thinking things through, and its underuse names someone who acts on impulse or first impressions without weighing evidence or consequences. Today that person is simply someone who does not stop to reflect before deciding.", "labels": ["Unreflective", "Thoughtless"], "gloss": "This means they act on first impressions and rarely weigh evidence or consequences before deciding what to do.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:judgment:overuse", "reasoning": "Judgment in excess becomes a habit of doubting every motive and dismissing every claim as self-interest. The person who has it today is a cynic who distrusts others and sees the worst in everything.", "labels": ["Cynical", "Distrustful"], "gloss": "This means they assume bad motives behind everything people do and dismiss sincere efforts as naive or self-serving.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:love_of_learning:strength", "reasoning": "This strength is a delight in mastering new skills, topics and bodies of knowledge. The person who has it is a lifelong learner who studies eagerly and seeks out new understanding.", "labels": ["Studious", "Eager to learn"], "gloss": "This means they seek out new skills and subjects with enthusiasm, studying steadily and enjoying the work of mastering them.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:love_of_learning:underuse", "reasoning": "Complacency is the underuse of the love of learning, a contentment with what one already knows. The person who has it today is self-satisfied and incurious, making no effort to learn anything new.", "labels": ["Complacent", "Incurious"], "gloss": "This means they feel satisfied with what they already know and never bother to learn anything new.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:love_of_learning:overuse", "reasoning": "Too much love of learning turns into displaying one's learning, lecturing and correcting others on minor points. The person today is a pedant who shows off knowledge rather than sharing it.", "labels": ["Pedantic", "Know-it-all"], "gloss": "This means they flaunt their learning, correcting trivial points and lecturing others rather than sharing knowledge helpfully.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:perspective:strength", "reasoning": "Perspective is the ability to give wise counsel and see the world in ways that make sense to oneself and others. The person who has it is a sound adviser who sees situations clearly and helps others understand them.", "labels": ["Wise", "Insightful"], "gloss": "This means they see situations clearly and offer sound advice that helps others make sense of what is happening.", "polysemy": true},
{"id": "via:perspective:underuse", "reasoning": "Shallowness is the underuse of perspective, grasping only surface features and offering thin views. The person who has it today is superficial, lacking depth of understanding.", "labels": ["Shallow", "Superficial"], "gloss": "This means they grasp only the surface of situations and offer thin, unhelpful views instead of real insight.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:perspective:overuse", "reasoning": "Too much perspective becomes pressing one's views and advice on others until they feel overruled. The person today is domineering, forcing their outlook on people who stop listening.", "labels": ["Domineering", "Preachy"], "gloss": "This means they press their views and advice on others so forcefully that people feel overruled and stop listening.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:bravery:strength", "reasoning": "Bravery is not shrinking from threat, difficulty or pain and speaking up for what is right. The person who has it is courageous, facing danger and standing up for principle.", "labels": ["Brave", "Courageous"], "gloss": "This means they face danger, difficulty or pain steadily and speak up for what is right despite the risk.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:bravery:underuse", "reasoning": "Cowardice is the underuse of bravery, shrinking from threat or challenge where courage is needed. The person who has it today is timid and fearful, avoiding what they should face.", "labels": ["Cowardly", "Timid"], "gloss": "This means they shrink from threats, challenges or pain, and avoid speaking up even when they should.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:bravery:overuse", "reasoning": "Foolhardiness is bravery in excess, boldness that ignores real danger. The person today is reckless, courting risk without regard for consequences.", "labels": ["Foolhardy", "Reckless"], "gloss": "This means they take needless risks with danger, ignoring the consequences in a rash display of boldness.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:perseverance:strength", "reasoning": "Perseverance is finishing what one starts and persisting despite obstacles. The person who has it is steadfast and keeps working toward goals through setbacks.", "labels": ["Persistent", "Steadfast"], "gloss": "This means they finish what they start and keep working toward their goals through obstacles and setbacks.", "polysemy": true},
{"id": "via:perseverance:underuse", "reasoning": "Fragility is the underuse of perseverance, giving up when obstacles appear. The person who has it today is irresolute, abandoning efforts at the first difficulty.", "labels": ["Irresolute", "Quitter"], "gloss": "This means they abandon projects at the first obstacle or setback and fail to finish what they begin.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:perseverance:overuse", "reasoning": "Obsessiveness is perseverance in excess, pressing on past all sense and being unable to let go. The person today is obsessive, fixated on a goal even when it harms them.", "labels": ["Obsessive", "Relentless"], "gloss": "This means they press on toward a goal past all sense, unable to let go even when it harms them or others.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:honesty:strength", "reasoning": "Honesty is speaking the truth and presenting oneself genuinely. The person who has it is sincere, open about who they are and what they think.", "labels": ["Honest", "Sincere"], "gloss": "This means they tell the truth and present themselves as they really are, without pretence or deception.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:honesty:underuse", "reasoning": "Phoniness is the underuse of honesty, presenting a false self and feigning feelings. The person today is a fake, insincere in what they show others.", "labels": ["Phony", "Insincere"], "gloss": "This means they pretend to be someone they are not, feign feelings, and mislead others about who they really are.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:honesty:overuse", "reasoning": "Righteousness here is honesty in excess, blurting out harsh truths and moralizing at others. The person today is self-righteous, smugly sure that their candour is always a virtue.", "labels": ["Self-righteous", "Moralistic"], "gloss": "This means they blurt out harsh truths and moralize at others, smugly sure their candour is always a virtue.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:zest:strength", "reasoning": "Zest is approaching life with excitement and energy. The person who has it is enthusiastic, throwing themselves into activities with real eagerness.", "labels": ["Enthusiastic", "Energetic"], "gloss": "This means they approach life with eagerness and vigor, throwing themselves into activities with real excitement.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:zest:underuse", "reasoning": "Sedentary is the underuse of zest, a lack of energy and drive, leaving life flat. The person who has it today is listless and apathetic, rarely excited by anything.", "labels": ["Listless", "Apathetic"], "gloss": "This means they lack energy and drive, going through life flat and unmotivated, rarely excited about anything.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:zest:overuse", "reasoning": "Hyperactivity is zest in excess, a restless rush from one thing to the next. The person today is hyperactive, unable to slow down or focus.", "labels": ["Hyperactive", "Restless"], "gloss": "This means they are constantly restless and overexcited, rushing from one thing to the next without rest or focus.", "polysemy": false}
]}

{"id": "via:love:strength", "reasoning": "Love as a strength means valuing close bonds in which care is given and returned. A person who has it today is warm and attached to others, and is open to closeness.", "labels": ["loving", "affectionate"], "gloss": "This means you value close bonds, giving care to others and accepting it from them in return.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:love:underuse", "reasoning": "Emotional isolation is love used too little, so a person holds back closeness even where it would help. Today we call such a person aloof, someone who keeps others at arm's length.", "labels": ["aloof", "emotionally withdrawn"], "gloss": "This means you keep others at a distance, holding back affection even where warmth would serve them and you.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:love:overuse", "reasoning": "Emotional promiscuity is love spent too freely on too many people, without discernment, so that closeness loses its meaning. The common word 'promiscuous' is mainly sexual, so the plainer phrase comes first.", "labels": ["indiscriminately affectionate", "promiscuous"], "gloss": "This means you give affection freely to nearly everyone, without discernment, so that closeness stops meaning much.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:kindness:strength", "reasoning": "Kindness here means doing favors and good deeds for others. A person who has it is helpful and generous, and does good without much expectation of return.", "labels": ["kind", "generous"], "gloss": "This means you go out of your way to help others with favors and good deeds, asking little back.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:kindness:underuse", "reasoning": "Indifference is kindness used too little, so a person lets others' needs pass without doing favors or good deeds. Today this is an uncaring person who does not bother to help.", "labels": ["indifferent", "uncaring"], "gloss": "This means you let others' needs pass without lifting a finger, even when a small kindness would make a real difference.", "polysemy": true},
{"id": "via:kindness:overuse", "reasoning": "Intrusiveness is kindness pressed too far, where help is forced on people who did not ask for it and their privacy is crowded out. {"id": "via:social_intelligence:strength", "reasoning": "Social intelligence is awareness of the motives and feelings of others and of oneself. {"id": "via:social_intelligence:underuse", "reasoning": "Cluelessness is social intelligence used too little, so a person misses what others feel and want and seldom notices their own motives. {"id": "via:social_intelligence:overuse", "reasoning": "Over-analysis is social intelligence used so relentlessly that a person dissects every motive and feeling, distrusting instinct and stalling. {"id": "via:teamwork:strength", "reasoning": "Teamwork means working well as a member of a group, being loyal and doing one's share. {"id": "via:teamwork:underuse", "reasoning": "Selfishness is teamwork used too little, so a person puts their own interests above the group, shirks their share, and lets others carry the load. The word is still in full use for such a person.", "labels": ["selfish", "self-serving"], "gloss": "This means you put your own interests first, shirk your share of group work, and let others carry the load.", "polysemy": false},
{"id": "via:teamwork:overuse", "reasoning": "Dependency is teamwork used too much, so a person leans on the group so heavily that they cannot act or decide alone. {"id": "via:fairness:strength", "reasoning": "Fairness here means treating all people the same by notions of justice. {"id": "via:fairness:underuse", "reasoning": "Partisanship is fairness used too little, so a person takes sides and favors their own group, treating others by different standards. {"id": "via:fairness:overuse", "reasoning": "Detachment is fairness used too much, so a person applies rules so coldly and impersonally that circumstances and feelings are ignored. {"id": "via:leadership:strength", "reasoning": "Leadership here means encouraging a group to get things done while keeping good relations within it. {"id": "via:leadership:underuse", "reasoning": "Compliancy is leadership used too little, so a person goes along with others and defers, failing to lead when the group needs direction. {"id": "via:leadership:overuse", "reasoning": "Despotism is leadership used too much, so a person rules by command, crushing dissent and disregarding others' views and the group's relationships. {"id": "via:forgiveness:strength", "reasoning": "Forgiveness means pardoning those who have done wrong and giving them a second chance. {"id": "via:forgiveness:underuse", "reasoning": "Mercilessness is forgiveness used too little, so a person refuses to pardon and holds grudges, denying anyone a second chance. ]}
